issues.description: The problem statement (UML and text) specifies orderMeal(Meal) as returning void, but the solution implementation defines orderMeal(Meal) to return boolean. This is a structural signature mismatch: students following the specification will implement a void method, while the reference solution uses a different return type. This can confuse students about the required method signature and cause incompatibility with any tests or autograders that expect the void signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent. Either change the solution's orderMeal method to return void (and adjust the implementation to not return a boolean), or update the problem statement and UML to specify that orderMeal returns boolean. Preferably change the solution to 'public void orderMeal(Meal meal)' so it matches the UML and textual specification.
